messages:
anya: Ran a profiling sweep on tp=8, 8xA100, 16k seq. Seeing ~1.1GB per-GPU NCCL comm buffers in the allocator trace even when batch_size is tiny. Uploaded timeline to S3.

mike: that seems high. is the memory sticky across steps or just a transient allocation during init?

anya: sticky across steps — profiler shows cudaMalloc at start for comm buffers and they never get freed. NCCL v2.11.4, collectives are reduce_scatter/all_gather.

tim: probable NCCL-staged host buffers or pinned buffers for IB verbs. what did NCCL_P2P_LEVEL and socket iface look like?

anya: env: NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0. Also noticed our attention kernel falls back to a different codepath for seq>8 which inflates temporary workspace sizes — might be compounding the footprint.

hannah: can you paste the profiler snippet here?

anya: ```
GPU0 allocs:
  cudaMalloc  1183MB  (nccl comm pool)
  cudaMalloc  256MB   (attention tmp workspace)
  cudaHostAlloc 64MB   (pinned staging)
GPU0 persistent resident after step 10: 1.6GB
```

mike: interesting — if NCCL is pinning host buffers then you can see big gaps. try forcing NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS (force PCIe path) to see if NVLink staging is the culprit.

anya: ran SYS test: per-GPU NCCL staging dropped to ~380MB, but observed ~2ms added latency per step. nvprof shows the cudaMallocs are still at init but smaller. Looks like NVL path pre-allocates larger staging.

dylan: hypothesis: our comm pool allocator is calling cudaMalloc for each slot instead of using a shared arena / cudaMallocHost region that we can reuse. fragmentation + lack of reuse leads to permanently-resident buffers.

tim: also check our runtime's "workspace sizing" heuristic — I think the kernel switch for longer seqs requests 2x workspace which forces the allocator to reserve different slabs (and we end up with both small+large arenas). That multiplies the comm+tmp footprint.

mike: small experiment: enabling runtime flag reuse-temp-buf-ttl=60s (keep temp buffers in an LRU pool for 60s) dropped peak by ~30% on the 8-GPU run. Not perfect for steady-state but good for burstiness.

anya: I sketched a test harness: /perf/nccl_comm_pool_reuse.sh and uploaded alloc traces + top-down nvprof flamegraphs to s3://redwood-perf/2026/1934567890/nccl-traces.tar.gz

hannah: thanks. can we get a quick PR with the TTL opt-in so we can run longer soak tests in staging? also add perf counters for comm pool bytes per-gpu in the console.

dylan: action items: 1) try using cudaHostAlloc + ncclReg instead of cudaMalloc for staging buffers (to reduce device-visible resident allocation), 2) test NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS vs NVL to quantify tradeoffs, 3) prototype reuse-temp-buf-ttl in runtime (opt-in), 4) add per-stream/per-gpu comm pool metrics to Console. I can take 1 and 3.

mike: I'll take 2 and 4 and run the SYS/NVL matrix across tp=4/8. @anya pls drop the raw nvprof logs into #eng-runtime-artifacts so I can wire the console panels.

anya: dropping logs now: s3://redwood-perf/2026/1934567890/nccl-traces.tar.gz :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy bench job started: build/bench-nccl-2026 (job id 3581) — running on staging cluster nodes 12-19.

hannah: let's aim to have a short writeup after the staging soak summarizing perf vs memory and recommended defaults for Dedicated. Keep it focused on: comm-pool alloc strategy, workspace heuristics, and a fallback policy (SYS when NVL causes big resident staging).

dylan: agreed. I'll draft a short doc and prototype the cudaHostAlloc path this week.

mike: noted. i'll add dashboard cards and the soak runs to the perf board.

anya: thanks everyone — will update the thread with bench results and PR links.
